sections.label: Road traffic Act amendments objectives
sections.summary: The Act has been amended four times since 2019, and three key objectives are sought today.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Since 2019, the Act has been amended four times.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: We seek to do so again today, to achieve three key objectives: First, strengthen accountability for the most egregious road conduct; Second, further deter driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs; and third, enhance the Traffic Police's ability to detect and enforce against traffic offences.

sections.label: Punishment for death caused
sections.summary: Where death is caused, the offender is punished with imprisonment up to 15 years and fine or caning, or both.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Where death is caused, the offender is to be punished with imprisonment, which may extend to 15 years and is also liable to fine or caning, or both.

sections.label: Dangerous driving causing grievous hurt penalties
sections.summary: The Bill raises maximum imprisonment for dangerous driving causing grievous hurt to seven years for first-time and 13 years for repeat offenders.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: For dangerous driving causing grievous hurt, the Bill increases the maximum imprisonment term for first-time offenders from five years to seven years, and for repeat offenders from 10 years to 13 years.

sections.label: Uplifts for serious offenders
sections.summary: Maximum uplift for serious offenders increases to one and a half years, and for serious repeat offenders to three and a half years' imprisonment.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: For both careless driving – also known as driving without due care or reasonable consideration – and dangerous driving causing grievous hurt, the maximum uplift for serious offenders will increase from one year to one and a half years' imprisonment.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: For serious repeat offenders, who are convicted of a dangerous or careless driving offence committed while under the influence of alcohol or drugs and who have a previous conviction for driving under the influence, the maximum uplift will increase from two years to three and a half years' imprisonment.

sections.label: Tightened prescribed alcohol limits
sections.summary: Clauses 11 and 19 tighten prescribed alcohol limits to 15 microgrammes per 100 millilitres of breath and 30 milligrammes per 100 millilitres of blood.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: First, Clauses 11 and 19 tighten the prescribed alcohol limits from exceeding 35 microgrammes of alcohol in 100 millilitres of breath, to 15 microgrammes of alcohol in 100 millilitres of breath; and from exceeding 80 milligrammes of alcohol per 100 millilitres of blood, to 30 milligrammes of alcohol per 100 millilitres of blood.

sections.label: New offence of driving with substances
sections.summary: The Bill introduces a new offence of driving with controlled drugs, psychoactive substances or intoxicating substances present in one's blood.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Second, the Bill introduces a new offence of driving with controlled drugs, psychoactive substances or intoxicating substances present in one's blood.

sections.label: New offence for specified substances
sections.summary: Clause 11 creates an offence for driving with a specified substance in the blood without separately proving impairment.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Clause 11 therefore introduces a new offence under the new section 67(1)(c) of the RTA, where a person who drives or attempts to drive with the presence of a specified substance in his blood will commit an offence, without separately proving that he was impaired whilst driving.

sections.label: Statutory defence for lawful consumption
sections.summary: The Bill provides a statutory defence where the substance was lawfully consumed or administered and the person did not know it could impair driving.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: The Bill provides a statutory defence where the substance was lawfully consumed by or administered; and the person did not know or have reason to believe that consuming it could impair his or her driving.

sections.label: Handheld Breath Evidential Analyser use
sections.summary: Clause 14 supports Traffic Police use of a Handheld Breath Evidential Analyser to obtain evidential-grade breath test results on the spot.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Clause 14 supports the Traffic Police's use of a Handheld Breath Evidential Analyser, allowing officers to obtain evidential-grade breath test results on the spot that accurately reflects the driver's alcohol level at the time of the offence.

sections.label: Removal of authorisation requirement
sections.summary: Clause 16 removes the authorisation requirement under the RTA, aligning it with the Criminal Procedure Code provisions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Clause 16 therefore removes the authorisation requirement under the RTA, aligning it with the Criminal Procedure Code provisions.

sections.label: Offence for holding mobile device
sections.summary: A driver who holds a mobile communication device in his hand while the vehicle is in motion commits an offence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: A driver who holds a mobile communication device in his hand while the vehicle is in motion will commit an offence.

sections.label: Automated traffic offence notices
sections.summary: Clause 21 introduces section 81A allowing a computer program to assess evidence and automatically issue notices for driver particulars.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Clause 21 introduces a new section 81A, which allows a computer program to assess whether there is sufficient evidence that a traffic offence was committed and if so, automatically issue a notice to require the vehicle owner to provide the particulars of the driver at the time of the alleged offence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: This enables the Traffic Police to significantly scale up the enforcement of traffic violations and eliminate manual processes, by using video analytics in traffic enforcement cameras.

sections.label: RTA disqualification period calculation
sections.summary: The Bill amends RTA provisions to make clear how driving disqualification periods are calculated.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: First, the Bill amends a number of provisions in the RTA to make clear how driving disqualification periods are calculated.

sections.label: Court of Appeal disqualification ruling
sections.summary: The Court of Appeal interpreted section 67(2) of the RTA to mean disqualification starts on the drink driving conviction date.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: The Court of Appeal interpreted section 67(2) of the RTA to mean that the offender's disqualification period should commence on the date of his drink driving conviction, despite the offender being in prison for unrelated offences.

sections.label: New dangerous driving offence
sections.summary: A new offence of dangerous driving to endanger another person on purpose causing death or grievous hurt carries mandatory imprisonment of up to 15 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: One of these is a new offence of dangerous driving to endanger another person on purpose that causes death or grievous hurt.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This new offence is understandably a serious one with mandatory imprisonment of up to 15 years.

sections.label: Mobile phone driving components reduced
sections.summary: The components for the offence were reduced from three to two: holding a mobile phone and the vehicle being in motion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Previously, there were three components that needed to be made out, but now there are only two – that the driver must be holding his mobile phone and the vehicle must be in motion.

sections.label: Alcohol and drug driving offence revisions
sections.summary: Alcohol-related offences reduce the required alcohol level, while drug impairment offences no longer require proving impairment or a minimum blood threshold.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Next, there is a revision of offences, first of all, in relation to alcohol-related offences, to reduce the level of alcohol required to make out a drunk driving offence, which I completely agree with.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: But separately, in relation to offences dealing with impairment for those who drive under the influence of controlled drugs, psychoactive or intoxicating substances, there is no longer a requirement to actually prove impairment nor is there a minimum threshold for the level of these substances found in a person's blood.

sections.label: Disqualification period and human review
sections.summary: The speaker seeks clarification on the policy intent for disqualification running after an unrelated prison sentence, and notes human review of notices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The assurance that these offences or these notices will be subject to a human review is also useful, certainly in the beginning when this is being rolled out.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I do have a final clarification of when the disqualification period will run and in particular, those who are suspended will have the disqualification run only from the time they have finished serving a prison sentence, assuming that sentence is for an unrelated offence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I would just like the Minister to clarify what is the policy intent behind this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Because if the idea of a disqualification is to keep the driver off the road for a certain period of time, why does it matter whether a driver is kept off the road because of a prison sentence or for some other reason?

sections.label: Traffic fatality and violation rise
sections.summary: Singapore's traffic fatality rate rose about 24% and traffic violations rose about 38%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Singapore's traffic fatality rate increased by about 24%, while traffic violations rose by approximately 38%.

sections.label: Maximum penalty and disqualification measures
sections.summary: Raising the maximum penalty to 15 years, default lifetime disqualification and vehicle forfeiture are appropriate expressions of deterrence and accountability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Elevating the maximum penalty to 15 years, instituting a default lifetime driving disqualification and empowering the Courts to order the forfeiture of the vehicle used in offence are appropriate expressions of deterrence and accountability.

sections.label: Minister reply on local studies
sections.summary: The Minister said no such local studies were conducted, and Rule 126 already makes distracting visual display unit installation an offence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: In a written reply, the Minister stated that no such local studies have been conducted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The Ministry instead noted that Rule 126 of the Road Traffic (Motor Vehicles, Construction and Use) Rules already makes it an offence to install a visual display unit in the manner that causes distraction or constitutes a safety hazard.

sections.label: Standards for in-vehicle screens
sections.summary: It asks whether MHA will work with LTA on standards for infotainment systems, app controls and screen-dependent cockpits, and restrict complex interactions while moving.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: In the interest of proactive road safety, will MHA work with the Land Transport Authority (LTA) to consider standards of governing pre-installed infotainment systems, vehicle mobile application control functions and increasingly screen-dependent cockpit designs?

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Will the Government look into whether we need to require certain complex touchscreen interactions or app-based functions to be automatically restricted while a vehicle is in motion, in the interest of driving safety?

sections.label: Vehicle-type approval for large displays
sections.summary: It asks whether LTA will consider evolving vehicle-type approval for large complex displays and whether safety-critical controls should remain readily operable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Against this backdrop, will the LTA consider whether Singapore's vehicle-type approval framework should evolve to better address the risk posed by increasingly large and complex in-vehicle displays?

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Does the Government agree that safety-critical vehicle controls should remain readily operable, without prolonged visual interaction with digital screens or navigation through multiple layers of menus?

sections.label: Traffic fatalities ten-year high
sections.summary: It states that the case for action is compelling and traffic fatalities hit a 10-year high in 2025.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The case for action is compelling, traffic fatalities hit a 10-year high is 2025.

sections.label: Penalty for road offence
sections.summary: The penalty reaches up to 15 years of imprisonment, caning and lifetime disqualification.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The penalty reaches up to 15 years of imprisonment, caning and lifetime disqualification.

sections.label: Work-related traffic fatalities reported
sections.summary: In July this year, it was reported that work-related traffic fatalities in the first half of 2025 exceeded last year's total.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In July this year, it was reported that the number of work-related traffic fatalities in the first half of 2025 has exceeded last year's total.

sections.label: One-time demerit points deduction
sections.summary: The Ministry provided a one-time deduction of demerit points so motorists avoid suspensions or revocations when the revised Driver Improvement Points System starts on 1 January 2027.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I am glad that the Ministry addressed the concerns by providing a one-time deduction of demerit points.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: This will ensure that motorists do not face suspensions or revocations when the revised Driver Improvement Points System becomes effective on 1 January 2027.

sections.label: Monitoring platform worker costs
sections.summary: The Ministry is asked to monitor implementation, such as account suspensions, and whether costs are passed to Platform Workers through fare adjustments.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: If so, I request that the Ministry actively monitor the implementation, for example via account suspensions, and whether those costs are quietly passed down to Platform Workers by way of fare adjustments.

sections.label: Medication and driver livelihood
sections.summary: A driver taking prescribed medication should not risk losing his livelihood, and the Ministry should work with pharmacies, doctors and Malay/Muslim organisations to convey information plainly and early.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: A driver who takes medication as prescribed by his doctor should not face the risk of losing his livelihood because of the very medication that keeps him alive.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I urge the Ministry to work not only with pharmacies and doctors, but also with Malay/Muslim organisations so that this information is presented in plain and simple language, that is conveyed early and to those who are most affected.

sections.label: New road laws and enforcement
sections.summary: The Bill penalises deliberate endangerment, makes standards stricter and modernises enforcement, and the speaker asks for clear communication, responsibility for livelihood risk and support for enforcement technology.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: It names and significantly penalises deliberate endangerment, it makes standard stricter for every driver and it modernises how we enforce our roads.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I ask that we: first, communicate the new laws and compliance clearly to the workers most affected before the enforcement begins; to take responsibility for the livelihood risk the Bill creates for compliant drivers and build in the transparency from day one; the implementation to support enforcement technology that we deploy to expand the enforcement power.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: As MHA itself noted, the road safety situation is worsening significantly, with the traffic fatality rate increasing 24% between 2021 and 2025, while traffic violations rose by about 38%.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I also noted that generally, the Singapore situation is also worse than some other comparable cities, with our traffic fatality rate in 2025 at 2.44 per 100,000 population.

sections.label: Silver Road and pedestrian survival
sections.summary: The Silver Road scheme reduced elderly pedestrian incidents by 80%, and a pedestrian hit at 50 km/h has a 40% chance of dying versus 13% at 30 km/h.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Silver Road scheme was found to have resulted in the reduction of incidents involving elderly pedestrians by 80%.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: A pedestrian hit by vehicle travelling at 50 kilometres per hour (km/h) has a 40% chance of dying compared with 13% when the vehicle is travelling at 30 km/h.

sections.label: Reduced alcohol limits for driving
sections.summary: Clause 19 introduces reduced alcohol limits, roughly 1.5 standard drinks for men and one for women within three hours of driving.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The reduced alcohol limits introduced by clause 19 signal new norms in another way to change the culture of driving in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The new limits are that permissible alcohol levels are roughly equivalent to 1.5 standard drinks for men and one standard drink for women consumed within three hours of driving.

sections.label: Helsinki road deaths and North Star
sections.summary: Helsinki had a full year without road deaths across 2024 and 2025 through lower speed limits, safer designs, enforcement and pedestrian infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: After all, Helsinki achieved a full year without road deaths across 2024 and 2025 through lower speed limits, safer street designs, strong enforcement and improved pedestrian infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It is time for us to set our own North Star in our own attempt to do so.

sections.label: New purposeful endangerment offence
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes the new offence of purposeful endangerment using a motor vehicle under the proposed section 63A.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: In particular, I welcome the introduction of the new offence of purposeful endangerment using a motor vehicle under the proposed section 63A.

sections.label: Removing phone operation proof
sections.summary: The Bill removes the need to prove that the driver was operating a phone.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: The Bill removes the need to prove that the driver was operating a phone.

sections.label: Stronger Traffic Police intervention powers
sections.summary: The speaker supports giving the Traffic Police stronger powers to intervene where reasonable grounds show a driver poses an ongoing danger.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: But because it has the potential to prevent greater tragedy.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: I support giving the Traffic Police stronger powers to intervene where there are reasonable grounds that a driver poses an ongoing danger to other road users.

sections.label: Safeguards for suspension powers
sections.summary: The passage asks the Minister to elaborate on safeguards ensuring suspension powers remain proportionate, transparent and timely.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Could the Minister therefore elaborate on the safeguards that will ensure that these suspension powers remain proportionate, transparent and timely?

sections.label: Lower alcohol limits
sections.summary: The Bill lowers the breath alcohol limit from 35 to 15 microgrammes and the blood alcohol limit from 80 to 30 milligrammes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Bill lowers the prescribed breath alcohol limit from 35 to 15 microgrammes of alcohol in 100 millilitres of breath and the blood alcohol limit from 80 to 30 milligrammes of alcohol in 100 millilitres of blood.

sections.label: New drug presence offence
sections.summary: The Bill creates an offence where a controlled drug, psychoactive or intoxicating substance is present in the driver's blood, regardless of quantity or observed impairment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Bill creates an additional offence where a controlled drug or psychoactive substance or intoxicating substance is present in the driver's blood, regardless of the quantity detected or whether impairment was observed.

sections.label: Hospital breath specimens and safeguards
sections.summary: The passage asks whether patient treatment remains paramount, whether specimens will be withheld if care would be compromised, and what training nurses will receive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: For hospital breath specimens, the person immediately responsible for the patient's care is expressly part of the statutory safety check.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Will the Minister confirm that the patient treatment remains paramount and that a specimen will not be taken where the clinician responsible for the patient's care believes it would compromise their care or treatment?

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: What training and professional guidance will be given to nurses involved in taking forensic specimens?

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Firm enforcement needs more than severe penalties though.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It must be grounded in evidence testing that can withstand scrutiny.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Clear rules on what constitutes drug presence and practical guidance for people taking lawful medication.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We do owe innocent road users laws that can prevent avoidable harm and ward off the next tragedy.

sections.label: Rise in traffic fatalities
sections.summary: Traffic fatalities rose to 147 last year from 139 in 2024, and red-light running accidents rose by more than a quarter.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Traffic fatalities rose to 147 last year, up from 139 in 2024.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Red-light running accidents rose by more than a quarter.

sections.label: Lower suspension points threshold
sections.summary: From January 2027, the threshold before a non-probationary motorist faces suspension falls from 24 to 18 points.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: From January 2027, the threshold before a non-probationary motorist faces suspension will fall from 24 to 18 points.

sections.label: Immediate suspension for speeding red-light drivers
sections.summary: A driver who beats a red light while speeding would be suspended immediately under the new regime, pausing income for full-time private hire drivers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: A driver who beats a red light while speeding would, under the new regime, be suspended immediately, and for a full-time private hire driver, that suspension is not a pause in convenience, but a pause in income.

sections.label: Spanish points restored for clean driving
sections.summary: Spanish motorists start with 12 points and can be credited back up to 15 after three clean years, prompting a request to consider a similar mechanism here.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Spanish motorists start with 12 points, but a driver who maintains a clean record for three years is credited back up to 15 points – a genuine, earned buffer built directly into the licence, not a separate reward scheme sitting alongside it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I would ask the Minister whether a similar mechanism, where a sustained period without any offences restores the variable demerit points, could be considered here, either for all drivers, or at minimum for our vocational drivers, who face the sharpest livelihood consequences and have the most to gain from a system that rewards years of safe driving with real headroom, not just a certificate and goody bag.

sections.label: Elderly pedestrians and motorcyclist fatalities
sections.summary: The 2025 figures show elderly pedestrians remain disproportionately represented in pedestrian fatalities, while motorcyclists and pillion riders account for more than half of all traffic deaths.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The 2025 figures remind us that elderly pedestrians remain disproportionately represented in pedestrian fatalities, while motorcyclists and pillion riders continue to account for more than half of all traffic deaths.

sections.label: Success measured by avoided tragedies
sections.summary: Success will be measured by families never receiving a late-night phone call, children crossing safely, elderly pedestrians walking without incident, motorcyclists returning safely, and private hire drivers earning while driving safely.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Its success will instead be measured by the family that never receives a late-night phone call, the child who crosses the road safely, the elderly pedestrian who walks to the Active Ageing Centre without incident, the motorcyclist who returns safely to loved ones at the end of the day, and I would add, the private hire driver who can keep earning a living while driving safely.

sections.label: One-year gap between hurt and killing
sections.summary: The Bill raises the penalty for grievous hurt to seven years and leaves killing at eight, a gap of one year given 149 road deaths in 2025, the highest in a decade.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I note that we repealed attempted suicide in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This Bill raises the penalty for grievous hurt to seven years and leaves killing at eight.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This gap of one year seems small, given road deaths last year were the highest in a decade – with 149 in 2025.

sections.label: Three-week starting point for unlicensed driving
sections.summary: Driving without a valid licence carries up to three years jail, but in PP v Eng Kwan Meng Garrick the High Court set a three-week starting point, suggesting the ceiling does little work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, driving without a valid licence carries up to three years jail.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This year, in PP v Eng Kwan Meng Garrick, our High Court set the starting point for a driver who had lost his licence completely and drove anyway, at three weeks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But three weeks under a ceiling of three years tells us the ceiling is actually doing very little work.

sections.label: Brake check licence suspension question
sections.summary: An MP asks whether the Deputy Commissioner of Police will immediately suspend a driver's licence for a brake check shown in video evidence before court proceedings.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Using the weaponisation of the vehicle to express your rage or whatever, is really not acceptable as it can cause dangerous accidents.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, when I look at the penalty, I am not too sure – maybe the Minister can clarify – that if a person or a driver has been identified and there is video evidence to show that this person has done a brake check, will the Deputy Commissioner of Police, who is in charge, do an immediate suspension of the driving licence before the Court proceedings?

sections.label: Highway code knowledge for road users
sections.summary: The Minister is asked whether he would consider regulations ensuring all cyclists or road users know the highway code.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Would the Minister consider passing regulations that ensure that all cyclists or any road users have a knowledge of our highway code?

sections.label: Grace period for mail offences
sections.summary: A suggestion is made to treat offences committed within a grace period of a few days as just one offence.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Another way is if we stick to the mail, then maybe we can consider that for a grace period of a couple of days – could be seven days or five working days – that whatever offence committed will be treated as just one offence.

sections.label: Temporary licence suspension for dangerous driving
sections.summary: An MP asks whether the Traffic Police can immediately and temporarily suspend the licence of a driver involved in such behaviour pending legal proceedings.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Not only can such acts lead to serious accidents, but a moving vehicle can undoubtedly become a lethal weapon.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I would therefore like to ask the Minister whether the Traffic Police can immediately and temporarily suspend the licence of the driver involved when such behaviour occurs, pending the completion of legal proceedings.

sections.label: Platform economy delivery riders on roads
sections.summary: The rapid expansion of the platform economy has brought many more delivery riders on the roads, many relying on Power-Assisted Bicycles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For example, the rapid expansion of the platform economy has brought about many more delivery riders on our roads, many of whom rely on Power-Assisted Bicycles (PABs).

sections.label: Technology against distracted driving enforcement
sections.summary: The Minister is asked how Singapore intends to use technology against distracted driving and whether automated detection systems will be deployed more widely.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In light of this, could the Minister elaborate how Singapore intends to leverage technology to strengthen enforcement against distracted driving?

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Will Singapore consider wider deployment of automated or automatic detection systems at high-risk locations or along major expressways?

sections.label: Mandatory intervention for repeat offenders
sections.summary: The speaker encourages the Government to consider a mandatory distracted driving intervention programme for repeat offenders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Such habits cannot always be corrected through fines and demerit points alone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I therefore encourage the Government to consider introducing a mandatory distracted driving intervention programme for repeat offenders.

sections.label: Distracted driving in curriculum
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether distracted driving could be a compulsory module in the learner driver curriculum and Driver Improvement Points System courses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Could distracted driving become a compulsory module within the learner driver curriculum before they are granted their driving license and likewise be incorporated into the Driver Improvement Points System courses?

sections.label: Early intervention for vocational drivers
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Government would consider an early intervention mechanism for vocational drivers reaching nine demerit points.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: More importantly, their driving licence is not just the privilege; it is also tied to their livelihood.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I therefore ask whether the Government would consider introducing an early intervention mechanism for vocational drivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For example, upon reaching nine demerit points, they could be required to attend a mandatory road safety programme focused on defensive driving, hazard awareness and responsible driving behaviour.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Upon successful completion of this programme, they could receive a one-time reduction of three demerit points, available once every two years in line with the existing demerit point cycle.

sections.label: Maximum penalty for new offence
sections.summary: The speaker states the maximum penalty for the new offence of purposeful endangerment causing death or grievous hurt is 15 years' jail.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: My starting point is this: the maximum penalty for the new offence of purposeful endangerment causing death or even grievous hurt is 15 years' jail.

sections.label: Penalty for dangerous driving death
sections.summary: The speaker states dangerous driving causing death carries a maximum penalty of only eight years, almost half the new offence's penalty.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: Yet, the existing offence of dangerous driving causing death still carries a maximum penalty of only eight years – almost half that of the new offence.

sections.label: Proposed higher penalty for dangerous driving
sections.summary: The speaker wishes the maximum penalty for dangerous driving causing death had been revised upwards to 11 years instead of eight.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: Using the maximum penalty of 15 years' jail for the new offence of purposeful endangerment as a starting point, I think the discount for dangerous driving causing death, should be no more than 30%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: And so, I wish the maximum penalty for dangerous driving causing death had been revised upwards, to 11 years instead of eight.

sections.label: Penalties for dangerous driving offences
sections.summary: The Bill proposes a higher maximum penalty for dangerous driving causing grievous hurt, still lower than for causing death.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: The culpability and harm from causing grievous hurt by dangerous driving may be not be less than causing death.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: This Bill proposes a higher maximum imprisonment penalty for dangerous driving causing grievous hurt, but it is still lower than the maximum penalty for dangerous driving causing death.

sections.label: Maximum sentences for grievous hurt
sections.summary: The Bill raises the maximum sentence for the worst grievous hurt incidents to eight and a half years from six.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: The High Court Judge sentenced Yoong eventually to five years, close to the maximum.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: But in his judgment, he also noted, "If anything, I wonder whether the maximum sentences prescribed are fully adequate for the worst type of incidents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: That is, however, a matter for the Legislature." Well, the Bill before the Legislature today provides one response to that, to the High Court Judge's comment, which is to revise the maximum sentence for these worst types of grievous hurt incidents upwards to eight and a half years from six.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: My view, as a legislator, is that for the worst type of incidents, where "worst" means surviving may not be better off than death; where "worst" means the grievous injuries caused are no less harmful than outright death, the maximum penalty for grievous hurt ought to be on par with that for death, higher than eight and a half years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: Or indeed, we ought to harmonise the offence for grievous hurt and death into one, as the Bill is already proposing for the new offence of purposeful endangerment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Last year, 149 people lost their lives on our roads, the highest number in a decade.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Between 2021 and 2025, traffic fatalities increased by 24%, while traffic violations rose by nearly 38%.

sections.label: Holding phone while driving
sections.summary: Under the Bill, simply holding the phone while the vehicle is moving becomes an offence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Under the Bill, simply holding the phone while the vehicle is moving becomes an offence.

sections.label: Tougher penalties for dangerous driving
sections.summary: The speaker supports tougher penalties for dangerous and careless driving causing grievous hurt.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Second, I support the tougher penalties for dangerous and careless driving causing grievous hurt.

sections.label: Vigilance to prevent road accidents
sections.summary: The law must stop dangerous conduct in time and the public must understand the risk.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Many road accidents happen in a split second.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: It may be a moment of impulse, looking down at a mobile phone, or thinking that one has not drunk much and should be able to drive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Therefore, the law must stop dangerous conduct in time and the public must also truly understand the risk.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Drivers must focus on driving; riders must pay attention to their surroundings and pedestrians should put down their phones and check the road carefully when crossing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: If each of us exercises a little more vigilance and think more of others, we can reduce injuries that could have been avoided otherwise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: We must remember that while roads can be travelled again, a life once lost cannot be restored.

sections.label: New offence for purposeful endangerment
sections.summary: The Bill creates a new offence with up to 15 years' jail, caning, lifetime driving ban and vehicle forfeiture.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Between 2021 and 2025, traffic deaths rose by about 24% and traffic offences by about 38%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Today, when a driver uses a car to scare or hurt someone on purpose, but we cannot prove intent to kill, the charge is usually dangerous driving causing death, capped at eight years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This Bill creates a new, tougher offence for exactly this conduct: up to 15 years' jail, caning at the Court's discretion, a lifetime driving ban, absent special reasons, and forfeiture of the vehicle.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: A car is not a weapon for settling scores.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I also support the tougher penalties for dangerous driving causing serious injury, the maximum rising from five years to seven years for a first offence; and from 10 to 13 years for a repeat offence.

sections.label: Automated Traffic Violation Notices
sections.summary: The Bill lets Traffic Police use an automated system to assess objectively verifiable violations and issue Notices without prior human review of footage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Traffic Police processes hundreds of thousands of violations a year, and today an officer must manually review every photo or video before a Notice to Furnish Driver's Particulars can be issued.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This Bill changes that: for objectively verifiable technical violations, speeding and red-light offences chief among them, the Traffic Police may use an automated decision-making system to assess the violation and issue the Notice without a human reviewing the footage first.

sections.label: Rising Traffic Violations and Fatalities
sections.summary: In the past five years, traffic violations rose 38% and fatality rates rose 24%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Indeed, in the past five years, our roads have become more dangerous as traffic violations rose 38% and fatality rates rose 24%.

sections.label: Mobile Device Offence Enforcement Amendments
sections.summary: RTA amendments let Traffic Police enforce mobile communication device offences using cameras or photographic or videographic evidence from the public, increasing detection.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: The amendments to the RTA aim to deter the use of mobile communication devices by allowing the Traffic Police to enforce the offence using cameras or based on photographic or videographic evidence submitted by members of the public, which will increase the detection of such offences.

sections.label: Clarifying Mobile Device Offence Position
sections.summary: The question asks the Minister to clarify MHA's position on such mobile device use and whether it constitutes an offence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Can the Minister clarify MHA's position towards such use of mobile devices and if they would constitute an offence?

sections.label: Public Evidence for Offence Enforcement
sections.summary: The amendments would allow Traffic Police to enforce the offence using photographic or videographic evidence submitted by members of the public.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: The amendments would allow the Traffic Police the enforcement of the offence using photographic or videographic evidence submitted by members of the public.

sections.label: Driving Instructor Mobile Device Rules
sections.summary: Driving instructors must set a good example, mobile devices must not be permitted during lessons, the curriculum should include past accident examples, and the basic driving test should include mobile device questions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: The driving instructors must set a good example and the use of mobile devices by both instructors and learner-drivers must not be permitted during driving lessons.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Also, the curriculum should include a module on examples of past accidents caused by the use of mobile devices, to let learner-drivers understand the extent of harm and damage that can result.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Lastly, the basic driving test should also include questions related to the "dos" and "don'ts" of mobile device use while driving.

sections.label: Support for stiffer driving penalties
sections.summary: The speaker supports amendments imposing stiffer penalties for dangerous and careless driving causing grievous hurt, specifically drink-driving and mobile device use.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin): Mr Speaker, I support the amendments to the Bill, to impose stiffer penalties on dangerous and careless driving causing grievous hurt, specifically due to drink-driving and using mobile communication devices while driving.

sections.label: Road traffic fatality and injury statistics
sections.summary: Police report figures show road fatalities rose from 107 in 2021 to 149 in 2025 and injuries from 7,240 to 9,955.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: According to the Police's Annual Road Traffic Situation Report 2025, fatalities on the roads rose from 107 in 2021 to 149 in 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: The number of people injured on our roads rose from 7,240 to 9,955 in the same period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: For example, while motorcycles formed only about 15% of our vehicle population in 2025, motorcyclists and their pillion riders were involved in 54.8% of all traffic accidents and accounted for about 53% of all traffic fatalities – more than half.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Our seniors constitute 12.9% of our population in 2025, yet account for 75% of all pedestrian fatalities.

sections.label: Holding phone while driving offence
sections.summary: The Bill makes physically holding a phone while the vehicle is moving an offence without needing to prove actual use.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Drivers may need to change the Global Positioning System destination, inform someone that they are delayed or deal with an urgent matter before continuing their journey.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: However, once the vehicle is moving, this Bill makes the act of physically holding a phone an offence, without needing to prove that the driver was actually using it.

sections.label: Lower alcohol limits and roadside testing
sections.summary: The Bill lowers breath and blood alcohol limits and allows roadside evidential readings, and the speaker asks how measurement margin of error will be addressed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: The Bill proposes to reduce the prescribed breath alcohol limit from 35 microgrammes to 15 microgrammes; and the blood alcohol limit from 80 milligrammes to 30 milligrammes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: The Bill allows the Handheld Breath Evidential Analyser to produce an evidential reading at the roadside instead of requiring a second evidential test at the police lock-up.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: But convenience must never come at the expense of accuracy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: I therefore ask the Minister how the margin of error for such measurements will be addressed, especially for the readings at or just above the legal limit?

sections.label: Standalone offence for road hogging
sections.summary: The speaker urges a clear standalone offence for persistent road hogging, listing objective factors to consider before prosecution.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: It contributes to unnecessary lane changing, undertaking, sudden braking, tailgating, road rage and may even delay emergency vehicles trying to get through.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: I therefore urge the Government to consider creating a clear standalone offence for persistent road hogging.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Such an offence should target drivers who remain unnecessarily in the overtaking lane despite having a safe opportunity to move left, who are not overtaking and who materially obstruct the lawful flow of traffic without reasonable justification.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Objective factors, such as how long the vehicle remained in the overtaking lane, whether it was overtaking, whether the adjacent lane was clear and whether traffic accumulated behind it, could all be considered before prosecution takes place.

sections.label: Line between danger and safety
sections.summary: The speaker says a clear line should be drawn between dangerous conduct and momentary safety acts, matching tougher drink-driving laws with reliable science, enforcement and prevention.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: We should draw a clear line between dangerous conduct and momentary acts done in the interest of safety.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: We should match tougher drink driving laws with reliable science, accurate enforcement and stronger prevention.

sections.label: Drink and drug driving changes
sections.summary: Clauses 11, 13 and 19 change drink and drug driving laws and create an offence for driving with specified controlled or psychoactive substances in the blood.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: First, clauses 11, 13 and 19 which enact changes to drink driving and drug driving laws.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: It also introduces a new offence for driving with specified controlled or psychoactive substances present in the blood.

sections.label: Holding mobile device while driving
sections.summary: The Bill removes the requirement that a driver be actively using a mobile device's functions, making it an offence simply to hold a mobile communication device while driving.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The Bill removes the requirement that a driver be actively using a mobile device's functions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: It will now be an offence simply to hold a mobile communication device while driving.

sections.label: New driving offences and camera evidence
sections.summary: The Bill introduces purposeful endangerment using a motor vehicle, raises maximum sentences for dangerous and careless driving causing grievous hurt, and lets the Deputy Commissioner of Police authorise a computer program to assess camera evidence and issue Notices.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The Bill introduces a new offence of purposeful endangerment using a motor vehicle, with penalties of up to 15 years' imprisonment; it raises maximum sentences for dangerous and careless driving causing grievous hurt; and it empowers the Deputy Commissioner of Police to authorise a computer program to assess camera evidence and issue Notices to vehicle owners for certain strict liability offences.

sections.label: Right to human review
sections.summary: The Bill gives vehicle owners the right to apply for a human review and revocation of an automated Notice.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: It is a tenet of justice that every citizen has a right to be heard by another human being before consequences are imposed on them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: It is for this reason that I am encouraged to see the Bill provide vehicle owners the right to apply for a human review and revocation of an automated Notice.

sections.label: Kinder driving culture and penalties
sections.summary: The Bill raises maximum penalties for careless and dangerous driving causing grievous hurt, tightens prescribed alcohol limits for drink driving, and makes holding a mobile communication device while a vehicle is moving an offence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I have met so many gracious people in our homes and in our hawker centres.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: And yet, too often, that kampong spirit disappears the moment we step behind a wheel – the driver who tailgates a slower car; the motorist who refuses to give way to a pedestrian at a crossing; the road user who treats every journey as a race to be won, rather than a space to be shared.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Our roads are not separate from our society, but are an extension of it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: How we drive is how we treat one another when no one seems to be watching.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: This Bill should not just be a set of legal amendments, but a mark of growth for us as a society that wishes to build safer roads and a kinder driving culture.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Hopefully, in the future, instead of "You think this is your grandfather's road?", we can all say, "This is our road".

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: It raises the maximum penalties for careless and dangerous driving causing grievous hurt, tightens the prescribed alcohol limits for drink driving and makes clear that when a vehicle is moving, it will be an offence for a driver simply to hold a mobile communication device without the need to prove that the driver was operating it.

sections.label: WHO estimate on mobile phone crashes
sections.summary: The World Health Organization estimates that drivers using mobile phones are approximately four times as likely to be involved in a crash as drivers who are not using a phone.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: The World Health Organization estimates that drivers using mobile phones are approximately four times as likely to be involved in a crash as drivers who are not using a phone.

sections.label: Road fatalities and handphone driving
sections.summary: A commentary highlighted 149 road fatalities in 2025 and failure to keep a proper lookout in 52% of accidents, and the requirement to operate a device's functions will no longer be needed for handphone driving.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: I was particularly struck by a recent Straits Times commentary by my colleague, Mr Krishnan Menon, from the Nanyang Centre for Marketing and Technology at the Nanyang Technological University.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: He highlighted that Singapore recorded 149 road fatalities in 2025, the highest number in a decade, and that "failure to keep a proper lookout" was identified in 52% of accidents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The requirement that the driver must also operate any of the device's communicative or other functions will no longer be needed to constitute the offence commonly known as "handphone driving".

sections.label: Bill and Driver Improvement Points System
sections.summary: The Bill and the Traffic Police's tightening of the Driver Improvement Points System from 1 January 2027 will mean more drivers caught, sanctioned and receiving more demerit points.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The passage of this Bill, coupled with the Traffic Police's announcement on 31 July 2026 that it will tighten the Driver Improvement Points System from 1 January 2027, will mean more drivers being caught and sanctioned, and therefore receiving more demerit points.

sections.label: Suspended suspension for drivers
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Ministry will consider a form of suspended suspension, such as a driving performance improvement plan or providing a sum similar to bail, for drivers whose livelihoods depend on driving.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In this vein, I ask whether the Ministry has considered, or will consider, a form of "suspended suspension" for motorists who accumulate the relevant number of demerit points.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: What I mean is this: especially for private hire car drivers, delivery drivers, passenger-ferrying drivers and others whose livelihoods are wholly dependent on operating a vehicle, could they, instead of or prior to suspension, be placed on a driving performance improvement plan, just like what my Parliamentary colleague, Mr Darryl David, has also suggested in his speech earlier, and/or consider for these drivers to be allowed to provide a sum with sufficient deterrent effect to guarantee good driving behaviour, similar to the concept of a bail?

sections.label: Public Defender's Office and phone distraction
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Government will review the Public Defender's Act to remove the RTA from excluded offences, and whether the Ministry is studying measures for phone distraction among pedestrians, cyclists and personal mobility device riders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The Public Defender's Office under the Ministry of Law currently does not provide legal representation to persons charged under the RTA, even where the individual who is facing financial hardship faces a potential term of imprisonment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In view of the increased severity of the penalties under this Bill, would the Government consider reviewing the Public Defender's Act to remove the RTA from the list of excluded offences in the schedule?

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Pedestrians, cyclists and personal mobility device riders who are distracted by their mobile phones also contribute to accidents and near-misses on our roads and footpaths.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I therefore ask whether the Ministry is also studying measures to address phone distraction among these other road users.

sections.label: Fengshan resident's fine appeal
sections.summary: A probationary driver and rider from Fengshan submitted an appeal because he could not afford the $200 fine and feared his licence may be revoked.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: Just yesterday alone, my Fengshan resident, a probationary driver and rider, Mr X, came to submit yet another appeal because he could not afford the $200 fine and was anxious that his licence may be revoked.

sections.label: Uniform $500 fine
sections.summary: A $500 fine is the same amount for everyone.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: A $500 fine is the same amount for everyone.

sections.label: Income-based traffic fines study
sections.summary: The speaker notes a person may have a low salary but substantial assets, and asks MHA to consider studying income-based traffic fines.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: A person may have a low salary but substantial assets.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: I am therefore not suggesting that Singapore should immediately introduce income-based traffic fines, but I ask for MHA to consider studying the consideration.

sections.label: Instalment payment framework for fines
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether a clearer and more accessible framework could let offenders facing genuine financial hardship pay fines by instalments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: Could there be a clearer and more accessible framework for offenders facing genuine financial hardship to pay their fines by instalments?

sections.label: Fines impact on lower-income road users
sections.summary: The speaker says fines disproportionately impact lower-income individuals and those earning their livelihood on the roads, and voices concern about this Bill's impact on them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: (In Malay): Notably, the impact of fines is disproportionate on individuals with lower-income and those who earn their livelihood on the roads While I support the intent of this Bill's amendments, I also voice my concern of the impact that will be felt by these groups.

sections.label: Income and obeying traffic laws
sections.summary: The speaker says salary or income should not determine whether a person must obey traffic laws, but notes some countries use income-based fines.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: Salary or income should not determine whether a person is required to obey traffic laws.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: However, there are countries that employ a system of income-based fines.

sections.label: Instalments and corrective alternatives
sections.summary: The speaker suggests a clearer instalment framework and that MHA consider corrective driving courses or corrective work orders alongside or instead of financial penalties or demerit points.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: Among them, a clearer and more accessible framework to allow fines to be paid in instalments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: MHA could also consider whether corrective driving courses or corrective work orders could be imposed alongside – or in limited cases, instead of – part of the financial penalty or demerit points.

sections.label: Causes of serious road accidents
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Ministry to share the principal causes of serious road traffic accidents in Singapore and how many involve speeding, mobile phone use, impaired driving, fatigue or disobeying signals.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: More broadly though, could the Ministry share the principal causes of serious road traffic accidents in Singapore?

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: How many involve speeding, mobile phone use, drink- or drug-impaired driving, fatigue, failure to obey traffic signals or other dangerous behaviour?

sections.label: Public reports outcomes
sections.summary: MHA is asked how many public reports lead to warnings, investigations or prosecutions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Could MHA share how many public reports ultimately result in warnings, investigations or prosecutions?

sections.label: Cyclist vulnerability with heavy vehicles
sections.summary: Investigations will determine circumstances, but it reminds of cyclists' vulnerability sharing roads with heavy vehicles.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: While investigations will determine the precise circumstances, it is a sobering reminder of the vulnerability of cyclists when sharing the road with heavy vehicles.

sections.label: Road safety beyond tougher laws
sections.summary: The Bill closes enforcement gaps on phone-holding, lowers drink driving threshold and recalibrates Driver Improvement Points System.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Because ultimately, road safety is not just about tougher laws.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: It is about ensuring that our convenience never comes at the expense of someone else's safety.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: If we can combine stronger deterrence, smarter technology, responsible operators and a culture of shared responsibility, we will not only have a stronger road traffic regime, we will have safer roads.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I believe that this Bill will close enforcement gaps by making phone-holding while driving an offence regardless of proof of active use.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I also welcome the lowering of the drink driving threshold to bring us in line with comparable jurisdictions and the recalibration of Driver Improvement Points System.

sections.label: More TVECs planned
sections.summary: After a pilot detecting over 67,000 violations in 11 months, MHA plans to increase TVECs on roads.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: MHA recently shared that after the TVEC's successful pilot, where they detected more than 67,000 traffic violations over 11 months, they have plans to increase the number for TVECs on our roads in the future.

sections.label: UK Pelican and Puffin crossings
sections.summary: UK Pelican crossings compel vehicles to stop, and Puffin crossings use sensors to hold red for slower pedestrians.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The United Kingdom's Pelican crossing pairs zebra markings with a signal cycle that legally compels vehicles to stop; its newer Puffin crossing goes further, using sensors to hold the signal red for exactly as long as a slower-moving pedestrian needs.

sections.label: Studying crossing models for School Zones
sections.summary: The Ministry is asked to study converting higher-risk unsignalised crossings in School or Silver Zones to such models.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Will the Ministry consider studying these cases for converting our higher-risk, unsignalised crossings in School Zones or Silver Zones to such models? : Sir, it is the responsibility of all road users to play their parts in road safety.

sections.label: Motor vehicle not weapon
sections.summary: The new offence of purposeful endangerment makes clear that a motor vehicle is not a weapon.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: First, the new offence of purposeful endangerment makes it clear that a motor vehicle is not a weapon.

sections.label: Lower alcohol limits, specified substances
sections.summary: Lower alcohol limits and new provisions on specified substances reinforce the commitment to keep impaired drivers off the roads.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Lower alcohol limits and new provisions on specified substances reinforce our commitment to keep impaired drivers off our roads.

sections.label: Warnings for first-time offenders
sections.summary: For lower-risk, first-time offenders with no immediate danger to public safety, the Ministry or officers could issue warnings where appropriate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For lower-risk, first-time offenders where there is no immediate danger to public safety, the Ministry or the officers could issue warnings where appropriate while helping motorists understand the new rules, especially for the cases where motorists are holding on to their devices.

sections.label: Reviews and published data
sections.summary: The passage asks whether performances will be regularly reviewed and whether data on notices issued and revoked will be published.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For example, will there be regular reviews of their performances and will the Ministry publish data on notices issued through automated systems and those later revoked after human review?

sections.label: Road deaths highest in decade
sections.summary: Last year, 149 people lost their lives on the roads, the highest number in a decade.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Last year, 149 people lost their lives on the roads – the highest number in a decade.

sections.label: Elderly pedestrian fatalities doubled
sections.summary: Elderly pedestrian fatalities more than doubled last year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Elderly pedestrian fatalities more than doubled last year.

sections.label: Motorcycle share of traffic accidents
sections.summary: Motorcycles are about 15% of vehicles but riders account for more than half of all traffic accidents.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Though motorcycles make up only about 15% of our vehicle population, riders account for more than half of all traffic accidents.

sections.label: Explanatory Statement on brain injury
sections.summary: One sentence in the Explanatory Statement describes traumatic brain injury causing permanent vegetative state as almost as serious as death.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: One sentence in the Explanatory Statement describes traumatic brain injury resulting in a permanent vegetative state as "almost as serious as death".

sections.label: Traffic Police road casualty statistics
sections.summary: Traffic Police statistics show 149 deaths and 9,955 injuries in 2025, with fatality rate rising from 1.96 to 2.44 per 100,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Based on Traffic Police statistics, 149 people died and 9,955 were injured on Singapore roads in 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Our road fatality rate increased from 1.96 death per 100,000 people in 2021 to 2.44 in 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This is an increase of about 24% in four years.

sections.label: Bill lowers drink driving alcohol limits
sections.summary: The Bill makes substantial changes to drink driving and impaired driving by lowering prescribed alcohol limits.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Second, the Bill makes substantial changes to drink driving and impaired driving by lowering prescribed alcohol limits.

sections.label: Detection certainty and enforcement cameras
sections.summary: The speaker says priority should be increased certainty of detection and asks if Traffic Police will extend enforcement cameras.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I believe immediate priority should then be increased to the certainly of detection.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: So, against this backdrop, could the Minister also share whether the Traffic Police intends to extend the use of fixed and mobile enforcement cameras, including on roads within our neighbourhoods at location frequent by children and seniors?

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: A person may apply for a notice to be revoked on the basis that the vehicle was not at the location of the alleged offence.

sections.label: Accuracy standards for computer systems
sections.summary: The speaker asks what accuracy and validation standards a computer system must satisfy before official deployment.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Could also the Minister say what kind of accuracy and validation standards that a computer system must satisfy before it is officially deployed?

sections.label: Road death reduction target request
sections.summary: A motorist asks the Government to consider a whole-of-government target for reducing road deaths and serious injuries with public reporting.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: A motorist should be able to return home without being intimidated by a larger vehicle.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Therefore, my final ask is this: could the Government consider setting a whole-of-government target for reducing road deaths and serious injuries with clear responsibility across agencies and regular public reporting on progress and measures that are taken at high-risk location?

sections.label: New purposeful endangerment offence
sections.summary: The Bill creates a purposeful endangerment offence for drivers who deliberately endanger others, carrying up to 15 years' imprisonment, caning, disqualification and forfeiture.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Bill creates a new offence of purposeful endangerment where a driver deliberately targets and endangers another person, such as through brake checking, aggressive tailgating, or swerving, resulting in death or grievous hurt.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This carries up to 15 years' imprisonment, possible caning, presumptive lifetime disqualification and vehicle forfeiture.

sections.label: Lower alcohol limits
sections.summary: The Bill lowers the prescribed breath alcohol limit from 35 to 15 microgrammes and the blood-alcohol limit from 80 to 30 milligrammes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Second, Mr Speaker, Sir, the Bill strengthens our impaired driving framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: It lowers the prescribed breath alcohol limit from 35 to 15 microgrammes, and the blood-alcohol limit from 80 to 30 milligrammes.

sections.label: Mobile device offence sharpened
sections.summary: The Bill removes the need to prove a driver holding a device was operating its functions and clarifies that touching a mounted device is not holding it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Third, Mr Speaker, Sir, the Bill sharpens the offence concerning mobile communication devices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: It will no longer be necessary to prove that a driver holding a device was also operating its functions and it clarifies that touching a properly mounted device does not amount to holding it.

sections.label: Automated driver identification notices
sections.summary: The Bill allows an authorised computer program to assess recorded images or videos and automatically issue notices requiring vehicle owners to identify drivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Fourth, Mr Speaker, Sir, the Bill allows an authorised computer program to assess recorded images or videos and automatically issue notices requiring vehicle owners to identify the drivers.

sections.label: Corporate vehicle owner records
sections.summary: The Bill requires corporate vehicle owners to keep accurate records of permitted drivers, including personal details, dates and allocation periods, retained for 12 months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Lastly, Mr Speaker, Sir, the Bill requires corporate vehicle owners, including companies, partnerships and unincorporated bodies, to keep accurate records of who is permitted to drive, including their personal details, dates, and allocation periods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: These records must be retained for 12 months.

sections.label: Digital logbook guidance and data protection
sections.summary: The Government should provide a digital logbook template and checklist before the rules take effect, with guidance on shared shifts, substitutions and allocation changes, and implementation guidance should address access controls, secure storage, safe disposal and data-protection obligations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: To help them, the Government should provide a simple digital logbook template and checklist before these rules take effect, with guidance on handling shared shifts, temporary substitutions and changes in allocation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Will the implementation guidance address access controls, secure storage, safe disposal and general data-protection obligations?

sections.label: Safer system and protected lives
sections.summary: The speaker says the result will be tragedies that never happen and lives protected, and calls for building a safer system and a society that expects and protects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: It will be the tragedies that never happen: the dangerous distractions designed out, the medication risk caught before the journey begins and the enforcement error corrected before it becomes an injustice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: It will be measured in the lives of the people we protect: the child crossing safely to school; the senior reaching the market; the delivery rider and the bus captain finishing their daily shifts; and the families waiting at home at the end of the day, who are not left waiting.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: But the refusal to accept preventable death begins with all of us.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This is our next step along that road, in our own way and for our own people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Let us take it not merely to write tougher laws, but to build a safer system and with it, a society that expects and protects, nothing less.

sections.label: Prosecutorial discretion over offence choice
sections.summary: Where facts satisfy more than one offence provision, whether in the same or different Acts, the Attorney-General's Chambers will exercise prosecutorial discretion to determine the appropriate offence to prefer.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
